title: 6 Fish I Won't Sell in My Own Shed — No Matter How Cheap I Can Get Them
description:
A salesman offered me pink fillets at $2.49 a pound. I said no thank you. Here are the 6 fish I won't sell in my shed — why, how to recognize them at the store, and what I sell instead.

1. Cheap imported "white fish" fillets (swai/basa) → U.S. farm-raised catfish.
2. The big old predators high in mercury (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, Gulf tilefish) → Spanish mackerel.
3. Escolar sold as "white tuna" → real tuna, labeled honestly.
4. "Red snapper" fillets you can't prove → buy it whole, head on.
5. Orange roughy → Gulf flounder, black drum, sheepshead.
6. Shark → mahi-mahi or cobia.

At any store: read the country and wild/farm raised, look for honest names, buy whole when you can, and if the price is too good to be true, it usually is. Fresh whole fish: clear bulging eyes, bright red gills, firm flesh, smells like the ocean.
